major.title: Major
major.body: Your main field of study, making up most of your courses. Many universities let you declare or change it after first year, so an intended major is a starting point, not a contract.

minor.title: Minor
minor.body: A shorter set of courses in a second field, on top of your major. It keeps another interest alive without switching programs. Requirements vary by school, so check your calendar.

double.title: Double major
double.body: Completing two full majors. It's demanding, and many students get most of the benefit from a major plus a minor instead.

switch.title: Changing programs
switch.body: Switching programs is common, especially in first year. Courses you've passed often still count as electives or toward the new program. An academic advisor can map out exactly what transfers.

transfer.title: Transfer credits
transfer.body: Credits you've already earned that count toward a new program or school. Ask the registrar's office which ones apply before you switch.

elective.title: Electives
elective.body: Courses you choose freely. They're built-in room to test-drive a new field before committing to it.

breadth.title: Breadth requirements
breadth.body: Many degrees require courses outside your main field. They're there on purpose, to help you explore and connect ideas.

advisor.title: Academic advisor
advisor.body: A free university service that helps you plan courses, add a minor or switch programs. Booking a chat before a big decision is always worth it.

coop.title: Co-op
coop.body: Programs that alternate study terms with paid work terms in your field. It's a great way to test a career before you graduate.

prereq.title: Prerequisites
prereq.body: Courses or skills you need before the next step. In Edventure, the lines between nodes show these.

branch.title: Branches
branch.body: Paths connect. A branch node shows a natural specialization, like CS into Cybersecurity. Following one doesn't erase where you came from.

mastery.title: Mastery
mastery.body: Going deeper on one skill through three stages. Mastering something gives you a foothold to jump into a different field.

crossover.title: Crossovers
crossover.body: Many careers live between fields: patent lawyers, health data analysts, UX engineers. Mastery unlocks these jumps.

match.title: Match %
match.body: How closely a path's key stats line up with yours today. It's a hint, not a verdict. Stats grow as you learn.

stats.title: Stats
stats.body: Built from your interests, courses and activities, then grown by completing objectives. Everything you earn stays with you if you change paths.

tiers.title: Stages
tiers.body: Rough timing from Grade 9 through first year. Move faster or slower: there's no wrong pace.

idea.title: Your own objectives
idea.body: You know what you want to learn. Add your own goal to any tree and it counts just like the built-in ones.

minortrack.title: Minor track
minortrack.body: When a path is your minor, the foundation and core nodes form a lighter track. Finish them to complete the minor.

goal.title: Your goals
goal.body: Goals you set in the quiz become ★ objectives in your top trees. They earn treasure like any other objective, and you can retake the quiz to change them.

compass: Changing your mind is part of learning, not a failure. Every objective you finish stays on your character sheet.
Electives and breadth courses exist so you can explore. Use them to test-drive something new.
A minor lets you keep a second passion alive without switching programs.
Your ideas count. Add your own objective to any tree, and it earns treasure like the rest.
Lots of careers sit between fields. Patent lawyers, health data analysts and UX engineers all combined two interests.
Thinking about switching? An academic advisor can show you what carries over. Talking to one is free.
You don't have to know your whole future. You only need a next step that interests you.
Curiosity compounds. The skills you build on one path, like logic, writing and teamwork, travel with you everywhere.
